method: Probes run inside a transaction against the owner's real Postgres, each setting role and request.jwt.claims to impersonate a specific caller — exactly what PostgREST does for a bearer token — so the policies themselves are exercised, not a polite client. Synthetic users are seeded to satisfy the FK and deleted at the end.

results.strangerForgesRosterOwnedByOwner: refused: new row violates row-level security policy
results.anonReadsRosters: refused: permission denied for table saved_rosters

cascadeOnAccountDeletion.method: A synthetic user was given a profile, a saved clash, a saved roster and preferences; the auth user was deleted; every owned table was re-counted.
cascadeOnAccountDeletion.verdict: every account-owned table cascades to zero on account deletion

remainingIntentional: rls_enabled_no_policy on schema_migrations (safe: readable by nobody)

cleanup: all synthetic users deleted; database holds one real account (the owner's) and no synthetic residue
note: No email, credential or personal field recorded. Counts and refusal messages only.
